Independent confirmation on **torch 2.14.0, CPU-only, Apple Silicon arm64 (macOS 26.5)** — the 6-line repro verbatim gives the identical **7/100 mismatched elements** between eager and `torch.compile`. So the regression is present on the current stable release across platforms, silently.

Given this writes wrong data (not just a crash), it's well-scoped by the report's controls — `masked_fill_` is correct and 2.9.1 predates it — and the `mutate_to` fast-path analysis plus the ready fix: please do open the PR.

issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```python
import torch


def f(x):
    y = x + x.sum(-2, keepdim=True)
    mask = y.roll(-1, -2) == y.transpose(-1, -2)
    y.index_put_((mask,), torch.tensor(7.0))
    return y


x = (torch.arange(100) % 3).float().view(4, 5, 5)
print((f(x) != torch.compile(f)(x)).sum().item())
```

```
7
```

Wrong on CPU and CUDA (7 of 100 elements here, 21 of 147 at 3 x 7 x 7 on CUDA), silently, and with `accumulate=True` too. On 2.14.0 `y[mask] = 7` does the same (the nightly traces that one another way and gets it right); `y.masked_fill_(mask, 7)` is right. 2.14.0 and the nightlies of 21 and 23 Sep are wrong, 2.9.1 is right.

The post-grad graph is fine (`index_put_(add, [eq], full)`, with `eq` reading `add` rolled and permuted). In the generated code the permuted read loads the buffer the fill is writing: the loop body of `buf1` has `ops.load('buf1', 25*p0 + p1 + 5*p2)`, and the C++ kernel does `transpose_mxn(out_ptr1 + ...)` with `out_ptr1 = buf1`, where it should read `buf0` (`add`).

I think this is `mutate_to`'s fast path. `index_put_as_masked_fill` calls `mutate_to(self, where(mask, value, self))`, and since `add` is not an input the fast path swings its StorageBox to the new value (`changed_data.data = val.data`). `add` was already realized (the roll's `index` needs it), so `y.transpose(-1, -2)` was lowered as a ReinterpretView of that StorageBox, and ReinterpretView's loader looks the buffer name up only when it runs, after lowering, when the name is already the fill's. The roll is only there to get `add` realized before the transpose is lowered.

Skipping the fast path when the target is already realized, and writing the value into it with `realize_into` instead, makes these right on CPU and CUDA. I have it with a test and can open a PR.

issue.title: [inductor] y.index_put_((mask,), v) with a mask that reads y through a transposed view reads the update's own output (regression)

timeline.body:
Independent confirmation on **torch 2.14.0, CPU-only, Apple Silicon arm64 (macOS 26.5)** — the 6-line repro verbatim gives the identical **7/100 mismatched elements** between eager and `torch.compile`. So the regression is present on the current stable release across platforms, silently.

Given this writes wrong data (not just a crash), it's well-scoped by the report's controls — `masked_fill_` is correct and 2.9.1 predates it — and the `mutate_to` fast-path analysis plus the ready fix: please do open the PR.

issue.body:
Fixes #198533
Fixes #198033

`mutate_to`'s fast path replaces the data of the mutated StorageBox with the new value. A realized StorageBox may already be referenced by name: by a ReinterpretView, whose loader looks the name up only when it runs, or by an extern kernel's inputs. Everything lowered before the mutation through those references then reads the new value, including the new value itself. With `y = x + x.sum(-2, keepdim=True)` and a mask of `y.roll(-1, -2) == y.transpose(-1, -2)`, `y.index_put_((mask,), v)` gives wrong values on CPU and CUDA. When an mm reads `y.t()` before the fill, the scheduler fails with a `KeyError`.

The fast path is now taken only for a StorageBox that is not realized. A realized one goes through the existing `realize_into` path, which writes the value into its buffer in place. Inputs, module buffers and NopKernels are all realized nodes, so their three checks are gone. Writing in place means two tensors must not share a buffer:

- The `copy_` and `fsdp.copy_` lowerings pass `share_value=False` to `mutate_to`, so the target gets a copy of the source instead of its buffer: if it took the buffer, a later in-place write to either would change both. `propagate_mutation` calls `mutate_to` with `share_value=True` directly instead of going through the `copy_` lowering: what it writes back (after an in-place collective, a mutable custom op or a user Triton kernel whose argument was copied to meet a layout constraint) is that copy, which nothing else reads, so an argument that is not realized can take its buffer as before. A realized argument now gets the copy written into it in place.
- An empty buffer that nothing has written yet keeps the fast path, the value copied into its layout, so `empty_like(x).fill_(0)` generates the same code as before.
- `realize_into` computes an `unsafe_alias` value (the in-place foreach ops) straight into the target only when the value reads the target at the position it writes, as an optimizer step does; otherwise the value gets its own buffer and is copied. This is the check of #198242 and applies to inputs too, so it also fixes #198033 (`torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)])`).

Writing in place also exposes a ConcatKernel bug, found and fixed in #198715: ConcatKernel computes a flexible-layout input straight into the concat buffer, so an in-place mutation of that input after the cat changes the concat. `index_put_` with integer indices after `cat` was already wrong; the masked form was right only because `mutate_to` swung the pointer. The fix is #198715's: GraphLowering collects the fake storages that some node writes in place (including inside control_deps subgraphs), and ConcatKernel copies such inputs instead of computing them into its buffer. The check is conservative on purpose: it looks at the inputs of the node being lowered, and a mutation anywhere in the graph counts. `test_cat_input_mutated_after_cat` and the two control_deps tests are from #198715 too.

Test plan, on 2.14 with the change applied at runtime, on CPU and on CUDA (RTX 4070):

- New tests in test_torchinductor.py: `test_index_put_as_masked_fill_mask_reads_target_view` (wrong values), `..._by_extern_kernel` (`KeyError`), `test_mutate_realized_buffer_in_make_fx_graph` (make_fx graphs that keep `copy_`, `fsdp.copy_`, `add_` and foreach ops, parametrized over five cases), `test_mutable_op_layout_copy_written_back_in_place` (a mutable custom op tagged `needs_contiguous_strides` gets a contiguous copy of a transposed intermediate that an mm has already read through a view; the copy is written back through `propagate_mutation`, and used to replace the intermediate's buffer), `test_cat_input_mutated_after_cat` (parametrized) and `test_masked_fill_of_realized_buffer_kernel_count`, which checks that a masked fill of an mm output stays one kernel written in place (Halide skips it: it won't fuse a read of the buffer a kernel writes in place). All 36 pass in test_torchinductor{,_dynamic_shapes,_codegen_dynamic_shapes}.py on CPU and on CUDA; without the change 20 of them fail on each. The ones that pass without it guard what writing in place could break: the `fsdp.copy_` case fails when only `copy_` copies, and the foreach case on an mm output fails without the check in `realize_into`. test_control_deps.py: 13 passed (the two new tests fail without the change).
- `test_inductor_steal_buffer` and `test_triton_kernel_clone_wekdeps` generate the same code as before. Across the collective, auto_functionalize, user Triton kernel and torchinductor tests below, `propagate_mutation` writes back 18 times, 16 of them into an argument that is not realized, which keeps taking the copy's buffer.
- A/B, same outcome test by test apart from the new tests: on CUDA (2,016 tests) the mutation/copy/fill/index_put/cat/concat/scatter/inplace/foreach/alias selections of the three files, test_inplacing_pass.py, test_auto_functionalize.py, test_control_deps.py, test_distributed_patterns.py (its `fsdp.copy_` graphs write a module parameter, a graph input), test_pattern_matcher.py's `fsdp.copy_` test, test_foreach.py, test_triton_kernels.py KernelTests, TestCollectivesInductor (single rank) and the cat/stack/index_put/scatter/copy OpInfo tests; on CPU (1,385 tests) the same files that run there. test_compiled_optimizers.py on CUDA: 805 passed and 3 skipped either way; the check in `realize_into` runs once per in-place foreach output, 150 times in the compile of a foreach Adam step with 50 parameters on CPU, 0.04 s in total.

Kernels and allocations, before -> after (64x64, the same on CUDA and on the C++ CPU backend; the mm is an extern kernel and is not counted):

| Pattern | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `s = x @ w; s.index_put_((m,), -inf)`, and `s[s < 0] = 0` | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| `fill_`, `add_` or foreach `add_` on an mm output, `empty_like(x).fill_(0)` | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| `copy_` of an mm output into an empty or unrealized buffer | 0 kernels | 1 kernel |
| `copy_` of an mm output into another mm output | 0 kernels, 1 allocation | 1 kernel, 2 allocations |
| foreach `add_` of `y.flip(0)` into an mm output `y` | 1 kernel, 2 allocations | 2 kernels, 2 allocations |
| foreach `add_` of `x.flip(0)` into an input `x` (#198033) | 1 kernel, wrong | 2 kernels, 1 allocation |
| foreach `add_` of another tensor into an input | 1 kernel | 1 kernel |
| A masked fill of `y` whose mask reads `y.roll(-1, -2)` | 2 kernels | 2 kernels |

The `copy_` and foreach rows on an mm output come only from graphs that keep their mutations (make_fx + compile_fx_inner): torch.compile functionalizes them away.

issue.title: [inductor] Don't swing a realized buffer in mutate_to

issue.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #198715

Fixes #198533

mutate_to's fast path replaced StorageBox.data with the new value, assuming
every earlier consumer was bound to the old Buffer object. ReinterpretView is
not: it holds the StorageBox and resolves the buffer name lazily, in its
loader, in get_read_writes, and in codegen_reference for extern kernel
inputs. So a transposed read of y lowered before y.index_put_((mask,), v)
was retargeted to the fill's own output, and an extern mm(y.t(), w) lowered
before the mutation read the mutated buffer. A ReinterpretView can only be
built over realized storage, so the fast path is now taken only when the
target storage is unrealized (the predicate StorageBox.realize uses), and
realized targets go through MutationLayoutSHOULDREMOVE.realize_into like
graph inputs already do. The old exclusions (input buffers, module buffers,
NopKernel) are all realized nodes, so the condition collapses to one check.

Routing realized intermediates through the in-place path exposed a second,
pre-existing bug. ConcatKernel computes flexible-layout inputs straight into
the concat buffer, so a later in-place mutation of that input (a reinplaced
index_put_ after cat) corrupts the concat. Integer-index index_put_ after cat
was already wrong; the masked form was right only because the swing wrote a
fresh buffer. GraphLowering now computes once, from the FX graph, the set of
fake storages any node writes in place, recursing into control_deps
subgraphs since the bucketing passes wrap already in-place ops there and
those placeholders carry the outer fake values. ConcatKernel.create refuses
to alias such inputs. The check is by fake storage rather than node position
so it cannot fail for cats lowered from inlined subgraphs.

Alternatives considered: binding ReinterpretView to the Buffer instead of
the StorageBox touches NonOwningLayout, MutationLayoutSHOULDREMOVE and
is_input_buffer and is far more invasive. Un-aliasing the concat at mutation
time would require every mutation path to detect NonOwningLayout targets.
PR #198549 takes the same route for mutate_to but calls val.realize() before
the check, which changes buffer numbering for fill_ on empty buffers. Cats
inside custom-op autotuning decompositions trace with fresh fakes and remain
unprotected, unchanged from before. The regression origin relative to 2.9.1
was not found: every lowering, IR and reinplace link on this path is
identical, and the wrong read hits uninitialized memory.

Test Plan:

New tests fail without the corresponding fix and pass with it, on CPU and
CUDA, under static and dynamic shapes. Previously wrong results on the issue
repro (5 mismatches CPU, 8 CUDA) are now 0.

```
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -q -k "mask_reads_target_view or extern_kernel_reads_target_view or cat_input_mutated_after_cat"
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor_dynamic_shapes.py test/inductor/test_torchinductor_codegen_dynamic_shapes.py -q -k "mask_reads_target_view or extern_kernel_reads_target_view or cat_input_mutated_after_cat"
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_control_deps.py -q
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py -q -k test_triton_kernel_clone_wekdeps
TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER=1 python -m pytest test/inductor/test_triton_kernels.py -q -k test_triton_kernel_clone_wekdeps
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -q -k "index_put or masked_fill or fill_ or copy_ or inplace or mutat or foreach or scatter or diagonal or cat or stack or empty"
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_inplacing_pass.py -q
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py -q -k "control_deps or subgraph or custom_op or invoke_quant"
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_custom_op_autotune.py -q
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_foreach.py -q
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py -q -k "buffer_mutation or mutat"
python -m pytest test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py -q -k "index_put or masked_fill or masked_scatter or scatter or cat or stack or (put and not input)"
lintrunner -a torch/_inductor/lowering.py torch/_inductor/ir.py torch/_inductor/graph.py torch/_inductor/fx_utils.py test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py test/inductor/test_control_deps.py
```
